delete_rule: Delete OTP scheduler harnesses after the VM-owned scheduler gate covers the observable behavior.

delete_rule: Delete Common Test/EUnit mailbox suites after equivalent VM process tests pass.

first_port_action: Port timer creation, cancellation, timeout delivery, sleep, monotonic clock, and timeout race behavior into VM timer tests.
delete_rule: Delete OTP timer app/library suites once VM timer primitives own the behavior.

first_port_action: Port process naming, lookup, unregister, duplicate-name rejection, and process-exit cleanup into VM process-model tests.
delete_rule: Delete OTP registry suites after VM process-model coverage owns the behavior.

first_port_action: Port link, unlink, monitor, demonitor, exit-signal, trap-exit, and down-message behavior into VM failure primitive tests.
delete_rule: Delete OTP link/monitor suites after VM failure primitive tests pass.

first_port_action: Port term/binary/string/list/map serialization behavior into executable Terlan std parity tests and VM value tests.
delete_rule: Delete OTP stdlib serialization suites once std parity owns the user-visible behavior.

delete_rule: Delete the Erlang distribution harness after the composed VM-owned distribution parity gate passes.

delete_rule: Delete only the external Erlang/Common Test harness and quarantined Rust source after equivalent golden-owned EPMD tests pass; retain EPMD discovery behavior independently from the Terlan distribution wire format.

first_port_action: Port TCP stream, accept, read/write, close, half-close, framing, and HTTP request/response behavior into VM TCP/HTTP gates.
delete_rule: Delete OTP inet/gen_tcp and benchmark-only harnesses after VM TCP and HTTP gates cover the behavior.

first_port_action: Port path, file read/write, directory, error, and permission behavior into executable Terlan std VM parity tests.
delete_rule: Delete OTP file/path suites once std VM parity owns the supported filesystem surface.

delete_rule: Delete OTP stdlib suites after each behavior has Terlan-owned parity coverage or an explicit unsupported diagnostic.
